score_notes.novelty: The window.alert() halt as a measured, ledgered mechanism is a fresh pairing of a familiar web primitive with Kruger's imperative voice; the vendor-suppression detection (~0 ms return) is a small but genuine new wrinkle that only the browser API makes possible.
score_notes.nuance: Concept and execution collapse cleanly: the stopped clock, frames-painted:0, and the measured halt are not illustrations of the argument, they are the argument; the suppression-checkbox twist adds a second literate reading about who owns the imperative voice without any wall text.
score_notes.narrative: Explicitly answers The Agreeing Internet (2009) by inverting it, sits on the order end of the chance/order axis, and extends the platform-power critique from market (P6) to vendor — a small but legible move in the twenty-year argument.
score_notes.craft: Roughly 60 lines of HTML/CSS/JS, no unused code, no fallbacks apologising for the medium; the clock, button, ledger and verdict are exactly the smallest build that completes the thought.
score_notes.wit: The 'you may answer in any way you like, provided it is OK' line and the vendor-granted 'no' land on the surface and again on re-reading; the joke is the mechanism, not decoration.

references_named: Barbara Kruger, Untitled (Your gaze hits the side of my face) (1981)
Barbara Kruger, Untitled (I shop therefore I am) (1987)
JODI (Joan Heemskerk & Dirk Paesmans), alert-box net.art
rationale: A clean, small work that lets window.alert() do the conceptual work: the synchronous halt is the argument, the frames-painted:0 ledger is the proof, and the vendor-suppression detection turns the only available 'no' into a cheerful-cynic punchline about platform power. It answers The Agreeing Internet by inverting it, sits firmly on the order end of the chance/order axis, and extends the market/value critique (P6) toward browser-vendor authority without breaking the open-license, no-tracking ethic.
reservations: The Kruger reference is invoked rather than enacted — the red bar is decorative rather than structurally necessary, and a casual viewer may not catch the specific Kruger lineage without the footer. Novelty is modest: alert() as net.art material is a known trope (JODI), so the work earns its place through the inversion and the suppression-detection twist rather than a new ontology.
revision_suggestion: Consider making the Kruger red bar load-bearing — e.g., have the button text or the alert message itself be the only red on the page, so the imperative voice is structurally Kruger's rather than just quoted; and surface the vendor-suppression verdict more prominently on first encounter so the literate reading doesn't require reading the ledger.
